clue.text: Keep arguing — like Mrs Sprat does

definitions.meaning: to keep up a long talk or wrangle, an informal idiom for chatting or disputing at length
in the nursery rhyme Jack Sprat could eat no fat and his wife could eat no lean, so she ate the fatty part

explanation.surface: A bickering couple compared with the nursery-rhyme wife of Jack Sprat.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack Sprat is from an English nursery rhyme: he ate only lean meat, his wife only fat, so she literally munched the fat.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to chat or argue at length, and taken literally it describes eating the fatty meat.

clue.text: Went quickly — to keep out of sight, it's said

indicators.note: the phrase signals a word spoken that matches the answer in sound

parts.note: to hide is to keep out of sight

explanation.surface: Someone hurried away to avoid being seen, so the story goes.
explanation.definitionFit: The archaic verb to hie means to hasten, so its past tense means went quickly.

clue.text: Courting ducks take wing outside

indicators.note: the word wing lies outside the ducks, enclosing them

parts.note: taken as written
a duck is a zero score in cricket, and zero looks like O, so two ducks are OO

explanation.surface: Courting waterfowl spread their wings outdoors.
explanation.walkthrough: A duck is a zero score in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: Paying court to someone in hope of romance is a synonym of courting.

clue.text: Stop at sea

parts.note: the nautical term for bringing a sailing vessel to a halt by turning into the wind

explanation.definitionFit: This nautical phrase means bringing a ship to a standstill with sails set against each other.

clue.text: Just beautiful!

definitions.meaning: an old poetic word for lovely

explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means equitable and impartial, and also attractive in an old poetic sense.

clue.text: Mouth-organs held in silence

definitions.meaning: the organs in the mouth used for taste and speech
people who stay silent are said to hold these

explanation.surface: Harmonicas kept quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mouth-organs' suggests harmonicas, but means organs of the body found in the mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: These muscular organs are in the mouth, and holding them is the idiom for keeping quiet.

clue.text: Stretcher bearer?

parts.note: a stretcher is also a brick laid lengthwise, so its bearer is a labourer who carries bricks on site

explanation.walkthrough: A stretcher is a brick laid with its long side showing, so the bearer is a building labourer, not a medic.
explanation.definitionFit: A building labourer who carries bricks in a trough on a pole would bear the bricks called stretchers.

clue.text: General still a Duke even if he lost his head

definitions.text: General still a Duke even if he lost his head

parts.words: General still a Duke even if he lost his head
parts.note: the British general was made a duke, and removing his first letter leaves the surname of jazz bandleader Duke Ellington

explanation.surface: A famous general keeps his ducal title whatever befalls him.
explanation.walkthrough: The Duke who beat Napoleon at Waterloo; without its W the name is Ellington, as in jazz great Duke Ellington.
explanation.definitionFit: The victor of Waterloo was a British general created a duke.

clue.text: Finished? Then I accept the offer

definitions.meaning: the one-word exclamation used to clinch a bargain

explanation.surface: Someone checks a speech is over before agreeing to a deal.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means completed, and is also the exclamation of agreement when striking a bargain.

clue.text: Flags put out in honour of a brave man

definitions.meaning: bunting hung up as ornament, festive adornment
a medal or award given for gallantry

explanation.surface: Flags are flown to celebrate a hero.
explanation.definitionFit: Bunting is ornamentation, and a medal awarded for bravery is also called by this word.

clue.text: It's used as antifreeze in bitingly cold weather

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the words bitingly cold, run together across the word break

explanation.surface: A remark about what keeps engines running in freezing weather.
explanation.definitionFit: This alcohol compound is the chemical commonly added to car radiators to stop coolant freezing.

clue.text: Sort of sight he encountered in the Alps

indicators.note: to sort letters is to rearrange them, so the words sight he are reordered

explanation.surface: A climber describes the kind of view met with among Alpine peaks.
explanation.definitionFit: Lofty summits and elevated places are what a traveller meets in mountain country like the Alps.

clue.text: Their union offers security

parts.note: reads like a marriage, but is a two-part clothing fastener whose pieces join to hold a garment shut

explanation.walkthrough: 'union' suggests marriage or a trade union, but is two small metal parts linking on a garment.
explanation.definitionFit: This two-part fastener closes a garment securely when the pieces are joined.

clue.text: Jogs for ages — it isn't bad

indicators.note: the letters of ages and it isn't are badly arranged, so are reordered

explanation.surface: A jogger insists running for ages does no harm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jogs' looks like running, but means prods or stirs into action.
explanation.definitionFit: To jog someone is to prompt or stir them, as one provokes or sets something in motion.

clue.text: Food the French may get unhappy about

indicators.note: the unhappy word goes round the French article

parts.note: sad means unhappy
la is the French feminine word for the

explanation.surface: French diners might get upset about their meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A dish of raw leaves and vegetables is a kind of food.

clue.text: A number, for example, press for some form of restraint

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty
to iron clothes is to press them

explanation.surface: A list of examples and a command to press, leading to a form of restraint.
explanation.definitionFit: A shackle fastened round a prisoner's ankle is a kind of physical restraint.

clue.text: Colour I call unusual

indicators.note: an unusual arrangement of the letters in I call

explanation.surface: Someone names a strange shade.
explanation.definitionFit: A pale purple shade named after the flowering shrub is a colour.

clue.text: It is well used by desert travellers

definitions.text: It is well used by desert travellers

parts.words: It is well used by desert travellers
parts.note: read as a fertile spot with water, literally a well, that caravans visit in the desert

explanation.surface: Something much used by caravans crossing the sands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'well used' reads as heavily used, but the place literally holds a well.
explanation.definitionFit: A fertile watered spot in a desert supplies wells that travellers drink from.

clue.text: Ring-road goes round a kiln

indicators.note: the ring and road letters encircle the letter a, so a sits within them

parts.note: a ring is round like the letter O
ST is short for street, a road

explanation.surface: A ring-road loops around a kiln.
explanation.definitionFit: A hop-drying building with a conical roof is a kind of kiln.

clue.text: Completely new sweet flavour

definitions.meaning: the herb flavour of peppermint confectionery

explanation.surface: An advert for a brand-new taste in confectionery.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes something in pristine condition and also the herb used to flavour sweets.

clue.text: Spanish snacks of cooked pasta

indicators.note: something cooked is altered, so the letters of pasta are rearranged

explanation.surface: Spanish snacks made from cooked pasta.
explanation.definitionFit: Small savoury dishes served in Spanish bars are known by this Spanish word.

clue.text: Ends interim arrangements

indicators.note: the letters of interim are given a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Temporary plans are being brought to a close.
explanation.definitionFit: Terminal stations at the ends of transport lines are plural of a word meaning end points.

clue.text: Bundles to haul on board

indicators.note: on board means inside a ship, so the hauling word goes inside the ship letters

parts.note: a ship is boarded, and SS is short for steamship
to heave is to haul

explanation.surface: Sailors must drag parcels aboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on board' is the convention for putting a word inside SS, steamship.
explanation.definitionFit: Bound bundles of cut corn stalks are called by this word, so it means bundles.

clue.text: Is embraced by a need for something aromatic

indicators.note: the word Is is held inside the letters of a need

explanation.surface: Someone in need finds comfort in something sweet-smelling.
explanation.definitionFit: The seed of anise is a strongly scented spice used for flavouring.

clue.text: Companion given a smile, causing annoyance

parts.note: CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British order
a grin is a broad smile

explanation.surface: A friend's smile turns out to be irritating.
explanation.walkthrough: CH = Companion of Honour, a British honour.
explanation.definitionFit: Vexation or mortification at a disappointment is a synonym for annoyance.

clue.text: It carries away the waste from a fish cleaner

definitions.meaning: a drain or channel that carries off rainwater and refuse
one who guts fish, removing their innards

explanation.surface: Fish waste flows away down a drain.
explanation.definitionFit: A street channel draining away waste shares its spelling with someone who guts fish.

clue.text: Temple ornament I'd made badly

indicators.note: made badly suggests the letters of I'd made are put together wrongly, so rearranged

explanation.surface: A craftsman admits to botching a decoration for a temple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Temple' is the side of the head, not a place of worship: a crown worn round the brow.
explanation.definitionFit: A jewelled band or crown worn on the head sits across the temples as an ornament.

clue.text: Take a meal up for the woman

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the letters are read upward, so reversed

parts.note: to dine is to take a meal

explanation.surface: Inviting a lady to dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's first name, so it stands for the woman in crosswords.

clue.text: Artist about to put up list

indicators.note: the artist letters go around the other piece

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

indicators.note: in a down clue put up means the word is reversed upward

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A painter is about to post a schedule.
explanation.definitionFit: A roster of duties taken in turn is a list.

clue.text: Hostelry needs approval for modernisation

parts.note: an inn is a hostelry
an ovation is applause showing approval

explanation.surface: A pub's facelift needs the regulars' applause.
explanation.definitionFit: Introducing new methods or ideas is the act of making things modern.

clue.text: Frenchman provides a positive answer about centre of gravity

indicators.note: the positive reply wraps around the central letter

parts.note: yes is a positive answer

indicators.note: the middle letter of the word gravity is taken

explanation.surface: A Frenchman says yes to a question about gravity.
explanation.definitionFit: A common French male first name, so this stands for a Frenchman.

clue.text: Asian long-distance runner has audition for commercial

parts.note: the Indus is a long river in Asia, a runner being something that runs
an audition is a trial performance

explanation.surface: An Asian marathon runner tries out for a television advert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runner' suggests an athlete, but it is a river; 'commercial' suggests an advert, but it is an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to trade and manufacture, this adjective is a close synonym for commercial.
